directAnswer: Bluetooth audio quality can be poor due to compression algorithms, interference from other devices, and limitations of the Bluetooth codec used.
summary: Understanding the factors affecting Bluetooth audio quality can help improve your listening experience.

sections.heading: Compression Algorithms
sections.body: Bluetooth audio uses compression to transmit data wirelessly. This can lead to a loss of audio fidelity, especially with lower-quality codecs like SBC.

sections.heading: Interference from Other Devices
sections.body: Bluetooth operates in the 2.4 GHz frequency range, which is shared with many other devices. Interference from Wi-Fi networks, microwaves, and other Bluetooth devices can degrade audio quality.

sections.heading: Codec Limitations
sections.body: The audio quality also depends on the codec used. Advanced codecs like aptX or AAC provide better sound quality than standard SBC, but both the source device and the headphones must support the same codec.

steps.title: Check Bluetooth Codec
steps.detail: On Android, go to Settings > Connected devices > Bluetooth, tap the gear icon next to your device, and check the codec. On iOS, you can check codec support through third-party apps.

steps.title: Reduce Interference
steps.detail: Try to minimize the number of active Bluetooth devices in your vicinity and turn off Wi-Fi if possible to see if audio quality improves.

steps.title: Upgrade Your Devices
steps.detail: Consider using headphones and devices that support higher-quality codecs like aptX or LDAC for better audio performance.

faqs.question: Can I improve Bluetooth audio quality?
faqs.answer: Yes, using devices that support higher-quality codecs and reducing interference can help improve audio quality.

faqs.question: Why does my Bluetooth audio drop out?
faqs.answer: Audio dropouts can occur due to distance from the source device, interference, or low battery levels in the headphones.

faqs.question: Are all Bluetooth codecs the same?
faqs.answer: No, different codecs have varying levels of compression and sound quality. SBC is the most common but offers lower quality compared to aptX or LDAC.

caveats: Audio quality can also be affected by the quality of the source material and the capabilities of the playback device.
